description.narrative:
Wezesha Women Initiative, with its mission to protect women and girls from violence through social-norms change and socio-economic empowerment, is uniquely positioned to address these challenges. Drawing on our extensive experience in social protection, economic empowerment, and emergency relief, we aim to strengthen community-led efforts to prevent and respond to SGBV in Kyangwali. By leveraging Uganda’s progressive legal frameworks, including the Refugee Act (2006), the Domestic Violence Act (2010), and its commitment to CEDAW, we seek to create a safer, more equitable environment for women and girls.
Wezesha will Conduct an inception meeting withstakeholders (community leaders, local authorities, GBV Working Group members) They will develop detailed work plans and reporting frameworks Conduct community dialogues on SGBV prevention. Conduct consultative meetings with stakeholders in Kyangwali RS and Kikuube District on SGBV. Hold awareness marches within the community Conduct radio talk showson SGBV prevention Media Team Broadcast radio spot messages on local stations Media Conduct social Media Campaign’s across X, Linked-In and Facebook Media Team Produce assorted informational fliers, banners, posters and t-shirts and Outreaches Provide psychosocial support to survivors through counseling. Facilitate survivors to access medical, legal, and shelter services from the referral pathways Case Managers Organize a High-Level Stakeholder Summit in Hoima City. Project Evaluation and documentation of the project activities Develop a final project report and share lessons learnt with stakeholders. Develop one project policy brief on SGBV Project.

participating-org.narrative:
WEZESHA was established in 2020 to enhance access to basic needs, economic opportunities, and social protection services for women and girls. We work with Refugee and Host Community population in Kyangwali Refugee Settlement (Kikuube District), Women in Business in Hoima City, and the post conflict population of Northern Uganda in Oyam and Apac Districts.
Amidst the COVID-19 lockdown in 2020, violence against women and girls surged. Getting food and meeting other basic needs became a daily struggle for most families. Menfaced pressure to provide for their families, leading to increased Gender-Based Violence (GBV). At this critical time, Husna BabbraKia Etum, the then Protection Manager at Planning for Tomorrow Youth Organisation (P4T) in Kyangwali, faced an overwhelming number of domestic violence cases. She used their emergency family savings to set up Wezesha Financing Scheme to support former market vendors to start over and grow their businesses through an Innovative Reverse Saving Loaning Program. Reflecting on the positive impact,the success of this scheme led to the creation of Wezesha Women Initiative (WEZESHA) in July 2020 and the subsequent non-profit incorporation in June 2022.
2.ACHIEVEMENTS
Currently, WEZESHA has positively impacted approximately 3000+ women, girls and children through advocacy, awareness and sensitization on Gender based violence and advocating for their equal rights and dignity in the community. WEZESHA has successfully engaged 100 women in consistent VSLA for economic empowerment, 30 women have successfully been trained in soap production and 05 children got scholarships through Wezesha Women Initiative.
3.INSTITUTIONAL PURPOSE
Vision: A society with an empowered woman kind leading a violence-free life Mission: Protecting women and Girls from violence through socio-norms change and socio-economic empowerment Purpose: To increase access to basic needs, economic opportunities and social protection services
Institutional objectives: 1. To facilitate progressive social norms change 2. To expedite justice to survivors of violence 3. To provide basic needs to the most vulnerable survivors 4. To provide hygiene and birthing kits for women <(>&<)> girls 5. To promote girl child education through the scholarship program 6. To provide life, business and entrepreneurship skills to women and girls 7. To provide access to financial services through seed capital and linkage credit facilities 8. To provide mentorship and inspiration to women and girls in business 9. To engage and empower men in the protection of women and girls in their communities
Field(s) of activity: 1.Social Protection 2.Women Economic Empowerment 3. Emergency Relief Services and Disaster Preparedness
4. STRATEGIC POSITIONING
Wezesha Women Initiative is located in Kyangwali Refugee Settlement and Hoima City mainly working with the marginalised women and Girls both in the settlement and the hosting communities. Other relevant social actors include: 1. Humanitarian actors like United Nations High Commission for Refugees (UNHCR), NGO’s and INGO’S. 2. Government actors like Office of the Prime Minister (OPM), Local authorities like Refugee Welfare Councils I, II and III. (RWC’s) 3. Community leaders like cultural and religious leaders. 4. Media and media outlets like televisions, radio stations, newspapers among others. 5.
